messages.author: a236d3d356ca53fd
messages.subject: geom_smooth + rstanarm?
parts:
I just noticed that this works

p<-ggplot(data, aes(x,y)) + geom_point()
p + geom_smooth(method = "stan_glm", se = TRUE)

but this doesn't 
p + geom_smooth(method = "stan_gamm4", se = TRUE)
Warning message:
Computation failed in `stat_smooth()`:
object 'weight' not found 

I guess rstanarm wasn't designed to work like this, but found it interesting that it could be so easy to change existing plotting to use Stan :)
Question 1: Did you know this would work?
Question 2: No need to make it work, but can you point to an example where I can add fit to the existing ggplot object? plot_nonlinear returns a ggplot object itself...

Aki

messages.author: fc5d3270037d7478
messages.subject: Re: geom_smooth + rstanarm?
parts:
Cool! I didn't know that would work, but now that I see it I guess it makes sense that it would. We didn't intentionally try to implement that but apparently nothing we're doing in stan_glm causes an error when applied like this. Cool. We might be able to get stan_gamm4 working like this too, but I'm not sure yet what is causing that error.

In terms of an example of adding a fit to an existing ggplot object, I'm not sure if this is exactly what you're asking but, for example, here's an example of adding a bunch of regression lines (one per posterior draw of the intercept and slope) to an existing scatterplot to show uncertainty in the estimated regression line: 

library(ggplot2)
library(rstanarm)
fit <- stan_glm(mpg ~ wt, data = mtcars)

draws <- as.matrix(fit)[1:100, ] # grab 100 posterior draws of the slope and intercept
p <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg)) + geom_point()

p +
  geom_abline(intercept = draws[, 1],
              slope = draws[, 2],
              size = 0.1,
              alpha = 0.25) +
  bayesplot::theme_default()

which makes the attached plot. 


Jonah
